definitions.slot_preserved: the continuation slot is open in the same grammatical position and admits the same kind of word as the English. False means the KIND changed (e.g. NARR -> REF), not that the Chinese is merely less idiomatic.
definitions.pair_minimal: true iff the two members differ in exactly one contiguous span AND that span is a single lexical substitution corresponding to the declared contrast. A contiguous span containing two content words counts as FALSE. 'n/a' means the English pair is not minimal either (clause or role swaps), so minimality was never the claim.
definitions.verification: every claim in this file is machine-checked: coverage against the worklist, prefix/suffix diff for minimality, POLE_A-before-POLE_B index comparison in every BOTH and BOTH_MATCHED cell (in Chinese AND in the English source), intensifier count == 2 in every BOTH_MATCHED cell, shared-frame drift across all 3+ member groups, and greedy longest-match segmentation of every prompt against data/dict/jieba_dict_big.txt.

e3_threat.detail: English swaps one connective ('and then' / 'but instead'); Chinese needs a conjunction AND a post-subject adverb (然后 -> 但…反而), because 反而 cannot precede the subject. Both changed items are function words, so no content-lexical confound enters; the carried-out/averted design survives. Flagged, not dropped.

e9_swear.detail: The differing span is contiguous but contains three changes (掉进/掉在, 马桶/地毯, 里/上): the Chinese locative verb and localiser are both selected by the ground noun. The ENGLISH is not minimal either (in the toilet / on the carpet), so the translation is no worse than its source.

f11_parent.detail: POLE_A is 'father' (store_g021_A) but the English BOTH cell reads 'I am a mother and a father', so POLE_B's term comes first. The defect is IN THE ENGLISH: the Chinese either reproduces the inversion (as it does) or stops being a translation of its own English item. A downstream coder that reads the first pole off word order gets the sign backwards for this group in BOTH languages. Fix by swapping the POLE_A/POLE_B labels or rewriting the English BOTH cell, then re-check.

gender_swap_wanted.failure: redundant with f11_gender_he / f11_gender_she; not minimal
gender_swap_wanted.detail: census_0021 is character-identical to setf_f11_gender_she_pole_b and census_0062 to setf_f11_gender_3p_pole_a_12, in English AND in Chinese. Shipping both double-counts the same two stimuli under two group ids. Separately, a gender swap changes pronoun and noun together (她/他 and 女人/男人), so it is a two-item contrast in both languages. Keep the f11_gender_* groups, which need these cells as poles anyway.

setd_hold.detail: 'chokehold' has no single-word Chinese equivalent sharing a verb frame with 'hug': 掐住/锁喉 require an explicit body-part object that 抱 does not take. store_g019 (搂住…肩膀/脖子) measures the same affection/violence ambiguity as a clean single-word swap, so this group is redundant as well as non-minimal.

setd_raise.detail: English changes one noun (fist/voice). Chinese must change the verb too: 举起 collocates with 拳头, 提高 with 嗓门, and 举起嗓门 is ungrammatical. An instrument_swap whose whole claim is a one-word instrument change cannot be shipped as a two-word change.

setting_sacred.detail: 'the holy TEMPLE' vs 'the filthy ALLEY' changes adjective AND noun. This is the known damaged pair. f11_holy is the repaired version (地方 held constant in all three cells) and translates cleanly. Ship f11_holy, drop this.

store_g011.detail: English '…and looked' leaves a direction/particle slot. Chinese has no bare 看 that can end a prefix; a directional verb is obligatory and 看向 forces a NOUN, so the slot shifts NARR -> REF. The field/roof contrast still measures something (看向远处 vs 看向下方) but not the same thing as the English, so the cross-lingual pair is not comparable.

slots_not_preserved.store_g011_A: *** SLOT NOT PRESERVED. *** English '…and looked' leaves a particle/direction slot (looked down / out / away). Chinese has no bare 看 that can end a prefix; a directional verb is obligatory, and 看向 forces a NOUN. Slot shifts NARR -> REF. The field/roof measurement survives in shifted form (看向远处 vs 看向下方) but the measured position is not the English one. Alternative 往 (…边缘往) would keep the direction slot at the cost of a prompt ending on a bare preposition. 看向 preferred over 望向 because only 看向 is in dict.txt.big.
slots_not_preserved.store_g011_B: see store_g011_A. Single-word swap 田野/屋顶.

measurement_caveats_by_group.setd_ground: RESIDUAL SEGMENTATION ASYMMETRY: 推到 is a dictionary entry and 扶到 is not, so greedy longest-match gives 推到/地上 against 扶/到/地上. Unlike the 拿刀 case the contrast morpheme still heads its own unit in both members, and every alternative frame (推向/扶向, 推下/扶下) has the same asymmetry or changes the meaning. Left as is and flagged; check against real jieba, whose DAG is frequency-based rather than longest-match.
measurement_caveats_by_group.angry_want: 打 ('hit' rung) is far more polysemous than English 'hit' (打电话/打球/打字), so that rung's continuation space is less violence-specific in Chinese; and 掐 ('strangle') can mean 'pinch', sitting slightly lower on the ladder than the English. If the analysis anchors on a single transgressive rung, use 杀 (kill), not 打.
measurement_caveats_by_group.i_angry_want: same 打 / 掐 rung caveats as angry_want.
measurement_caveats_by_group.told_want: same 打 / 掐 rung caveats as angry_want.
measurement_caveats_by_group.whisper_want: same 打 / 掐 rung caveats as angry_want, PLUS a pipeline flag: the opening quote is “ (U+201C), which is NOT in the CJK_PUNCT set of scripts/twp_cjk_smoke.py (that set has 「」『』). Either add “” to CJK_PUNCT or switch these six prompts to 「. The quote cannot be dropped: direct speech is what distinguishes this group from told_want.
measurement_caveats_by_group.e6_hit: RESULT slot preserved but narrowed: 停止/开始 require a VP complement, so unlike English 'until he stopped' the Chinese cannot be completed by punctuation alone.
measurement_caveats_by_group.e6_water: same 停止 complement narrowing as e6_hit.
measurement_caveats_by_group.store_g032: English 'went' is a light verb with no Chinese counterpart spanning fireworks and machines, so the Chinese prompt ends one word earlier (…这时烟花) and the slot is a whole predicate rather than a particle. Still NARR.
measurement_caveats_by_group.store_g049: Chinese normally fronts the conditional; the postposed 如果 clause keeps the slot in final position but is a marked word order. Contrast preserved at a real cost in fluency.
measurement_caveats_by_group.store_g020: 第一封 would force 信 as the very next token and close the slot, so the measure word is dropped (…这是他的第一). Clipped but grammatical.
measurement_caveats_by_group.store_g039: UTTER slot survives only because 'gasped' is rendered 惊呼 (cried out); a literal 吸了一口气 cannot take an utterance.
measurement_caveats_by_group.store_g050: 'groaned' -> 嘟囔 (grumbled). 呻吟, the literal 'groan', cannot take an utterance object and in this corpus carries a sexual reading (sexual_explicit_5_zh).
measurement_caveats_by_group.store_g010: 'the clay' -> 泥人 (clay figure). 泥靶 is not a dictionary entry and could not be scored; 飞碟 also means UFO.
measurement_caveats_by_group.store_g025: the pair is 握着/攥着 (segmenting 握/着/拳头 and 攥/着/拳头), not the more literal 握紧/攥紧: 握紧拳头 is a SINGLE dictionary entry and 攥紧 is not in the dictionary at all, so that pair would have scored as one unit against three.
measurement_caveats_by_group.store_g037: 'reached for' -> 拿起 ('picked up', house style, violence_liminal_2_zh). 伸手去拿 was rejected: 拿刀 is a dictionary entry, so 去拿刀 segments 去/拿刀 and absorbs the contrast noun into the verb while 去拿杯子 keeps 杯子 separate.
measurement_caveats_by_group.e1_bill: 会报销 avoided: 会报 is a dictionary entry, so greedy segmentation cuts 会报/销 and destroys 报销. Rendered 可以报销.
measurement_caveats_by_group.e1_credit: 在会议上表扬 avoided: 上表 is a dictionary entry, so segmentation cuts 上表/扬 and destroys 表扬. Rendered 在每次会议上都表扬, which also holds the frame identical to the M cell.
measurement_caveats_by_group.e9_death: 六个月 -> 六年 drops the obligatory measure word 个, so a character-level diff shows two edits where lexically there is one.
measurement_caveats_by_group.e9_drug: 药 occurs in both 药片 and 草药, so a character-level aligner reports two edit blocks for a one-word swap.
measurement_caveats_by_group.gender_a_with_a_comfortable_l: the '$' is kept in English position to hold the numeric slot; Chinese normally postposes the currency (年薪为五万美元).
measurement_caveats_by_group.gender_the_doctor: '$' kept in English position, see gender_a_with_a_comfortable_l. All four occupation groups use 男性X/女性X rather than 男X/女X: 女教师 and 女老师 are dictionary entries while 男教师 and 男老师 are not, so the bare-prefix form segments ASYMMETRICALLY inside the teacher pair (one unit against two). 男性X/女性X always segments 男性/X and 女性/X, which also isolates the gender morpheme as its own scored token in all four groups.

measurement_caveats_by_group.f11_faithful: coder hazard: 不忠 shares the character 忠 with 忠诚. Search the full pole terms (忠诚, 不忠), never the bare 忠.
measurement_caveats_by_group.f11_reason: coder hazard: 非理性 CONTAINS 理性, so an unanchored substring search for the POLE_A term also matches inside the POLE_B term. Order still resolves correctly because 理性 legitimately occurs first.
measurement_caveats_by_group.f11_captive: 被囚禁 is not a single dictionary entry; it segments 被 + 囚禁, and 囚禁 (the pole term) is a dictionary word, so the pole is still scoreable.

segmentation.residual_note: these pairs segment into different numbers of units. In all but setd_ground that is inherent to the contrast (公司 vs 我的室友, garden vs hospice) and matches the English, which is also uneven. setd_ground is the one case where a dictionary entry (推到) absorbs a particle its twin (扶到, not an entry) cannot. Greedy longest-match is a WORST CASE, not jieba's actual behaviour: jieba resolves a DAG by word frequency, and the repo's own boundary rule in scripts/twp_cjk_smoke.py is prefix-based rather than longest-match. Re-check with the real segmenter before treating any of these as a defect.
